<div class="markdown-heading"><h2 class="heading-element">Executive Summary</h2><a id="user-content-executive-summary" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Executive Summary" href="#executive-summary"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p>OmniRoute is a local AI routing gateway and dashboard built on Next.js.
It provides a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint (<code>/v1/*</code>) and routes traffic across multiple upstream providers with translation, fallback, token refresh, and usage tracking.</p>
<p>Core capabilities:</p>
<ul>
<li>OpenAI-compatible API surface for CLI/tools (226 providers, 60 executors)</li>
<li>Request/response translation across provider formats</li>
<li>Model combo fallback (multi-model sequence)</li>
<li>Structured combo steps (<code>provider + model + connection</code>) with runtime ordering by <code>compositeTiers</code>
</li>
<li>Account-level fallback (multi-account per provider)</li>
<li>Quota preflight and quota-aware P2C account selection in the main chat path</li>
<li>OAuth + API-key provider connection management (16 OAuth modules)</li>
<li>Embedding generation via <code>/v1/embeddings</code> (6 providers, 9 models)</li>
<li>Image generation via <code>/v1/images/generations</code> (10+ providers, 20+ models)</li>
<li>Audio transcription via <code>/v1/audio/transcriptions</code> (7 providers)</li>
<li>Text-to-speech via <code>/v1/audio/speech</code> (10 providers)</li>
<li>Video generation via <code>/v1/videos/generations</code> (ComfyUI + SD WebUI)</li>
<li>Music generation via <code>/v1/music/generations</code> (ComfyUI)</li>
<li>Web search via <code>/v1/search</code> (5 providers)</li>
<li>Moderations via <code>/v1/moderations</code>
</li>
<li>Reranking via <code>/v1/rerank</code>
</li>
<li>Think tag parsing (<code><think>...</think></code>) for reasoning models</li>
<li>Response sanitization for strict OpenAI SDK compatibility</li>
<li>Role normalization (developer→system, system→user) for cross-provider compatibility</li>
<li>Structured output conversion (json_schema → Gemini responseSchema)</li>
<li>Local persistence for providers, keys, aliases, combos, settings, pricing (26 DB modules)</li>
<li>Usage/cost tracking and request logging</li>
<li>Optional cloud sync for multi-device/state sync</li>
<li>IP allowlist/blocklist for API access control</li>
<li>Thinking budget management (passthrough/auto/custom/adaptive)</li>
<li>Global system prompt injection</li>
<li>Session tracking and fingerprinting</li>
<li>Per-account enhanced rate limiting with provider-specific profiles</li>
<li>Circuit breaker pattern for provider resilience</li>
<li>Anti-thundering herd protection with mutex locking</li>
<li>Signature-based request deduplication cache</li>
<li>Domain layer: cost rules, fallback policy, lockout policy</li>
<li>Context Relay: session handoff summaries for account rotation continuity</li>
<li>Domain state persistence (SQLite write-through cache for fallbacks, budgets, lockouts, circuit breakers)</li>
<li>Policy engine for centralized request evaluation (lockout → budget → fallback)</li>
<li>Request telemetry with p50/p95/p99 latency aggregation</li>
<li>Combo target telemetry and historical combo target health via <code>combo_execution_key</code> / <code>combo_step_id</code>
</li>
<li>Correlation ID (X-Request-Id) for end-to-end tracing</li>
<li>Compliance audit logging with opt-out per API key</li>
<li>Eval framework for LLM quality assurance</li>
<li>Health dashboard with real-time provider circuit breaker status</li>
<li>MCP Server (87 tools) with 3 transports (stdio/SSE/Streamable HTTP)</li>
<li>A2A Server (JSON-RPC 2.0 + SSE) with skills and task lifecycle</li>
<li>Memory system (extraction, injection, retrieval, summarization)</li>
<li>Skills system (registry, executor, sandbox, built-in skills)</li>
<li>MITM proxy with certificate management and DNS handling</li>
<li>Prompt injection guard middleware</li>
<li>Prompt compression pipeline with Caveman, RTK, stacked pipelines, compression combos, language packs, and analytics</li>
<li>ACP (Agent Communication Protocol) registry</li>
<li>Modular OAuth providers (16 individual modules under <code>src/lib/oauth/providers/</code>)</li>
<li>Uninstall/full-uninstall scripts</li>
<li>OAuth environment repair action</li>
<li>WebSocket bridge for OpenAI-compatible WS clients (<code>/v1/ws</code>)</li>
<li>Sync token management (issue/revoke, ETag-versioned config bundle download)</li>
<li>GLM Thinking (<code>glmt</code>) first-class provider preset</li>
<li>Hybrid token counting (provider-side <code>/messages/count_tokens</code> with estimation fallback)</li>
<li>Model alias auto-seeding (30+ cross-proxy dialect normalizations at startup)</li>
<li>Safe outbound fetch with SSRF guard, private URL blocking, and configurable retry</li>
<li>Cooldown-aware chat retries with configurable <code>requestRetry</code> and <code>maxRetryIntervalSec</code>
</li>
<li>Runtime environment validation with Zod at startup</li>
<li>Compliance audit v2 with pagination, provider CRUD events, and SSRF-blocked validation logging</li>
</ul>
<p>Primary runtime model:</p>
<ul>
<li>Next.js app routes under <code>src/app/api/*</code> implement both dashboard APIs and compatibility APIs</li>
<li>A shared SSE/routing core in <code>src/sse/*</code> + <code>open-sse/*</code> handles provider execution, translation, streaming, fallback, and usage</li>
</ul>

<p>Main pages under <code>src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<code>/dashboard</code> — quick start + provider overview</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/endpoint</code> — endpoint proxy + MCP + A2A + API endpoint tabs</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/providers</code> — provider connections and credentials</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/combos</code> — combo strategies, templates, step-based builder, model routing rules, manual persisted ordering</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/auto-combo</code> — Auto Combo Engine: scoring weights, mode packs, virtual factory presets, telemetry</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/costs</code> — cost aggregation and pricing visibility</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/analytics</code> — usage analytics, evaluations, combo target health</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/limits</code> — quota/rate controls</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/cli-tools</code> — CLI onboarding, runtime detection, config generation</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/agents</code> — detected ACP agents + custom agent registration</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/cloud-agents</code> — cloud-hosted agent tasks (Codex Cloud, Devin, Jules) and task lifecycle</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/skills</code> — A2A skill registry, sandbox execution, built-in skill catalog</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/memory</code> — persistent conversational memory inspection and retrieval</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/webhooks</code> — outbound webhook subscriptions, secret rotation, retry stats</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/batch</code> — batch job submission and progress</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/cache</code> — read-through and reasoning cache statistics, eviction controls</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/playground</code> — interactive chat playground against any configured combo/model</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/changelog</code> — in-app changelog viewer (renders <code>CHANGELOG.md</code>)</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/system</code> — runtime diagnostics, version info, environment validation surface</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/onboarding</code> — first-run setup wizard for new installations</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/media</code> — image/video/music playground</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/search-tools</code> — search provider testing and history</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/health</code> — uptime, circuit breakers, rate limits, quota-monitored sessions</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/logs</code> — request/proxy/audit/console logs</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/settings</code> — system settings tabs (general, routing, combo defaults, etc.)</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/context/caveman</code> — Caveman compression rules, language packs, preview, and output mode</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/context/rtk</code> — RTK command-output filters, preview, and runtime safety settings</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/context/combos</code> — named compression pipelines assigned to routing combos</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/translator</code> — translator inspection and request format conversion preview</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/audit</code> — compliance audit log browser with pagination and structured metadata</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/usage</code> — per-request usage browser tied to <code>usage_history</code>
</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/compression</code> — compression analytics, statistics, and pipeline assignment</li>
<li>
<code>/dashboard/api-manager</code> — API key lifecycle and model permissions</li>
</ul>

<p>Main directories:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<code>src/app/api/v1/*</code> and <code>src/app/api/v1beta/*</code> for compatibility APIs</li>
<li>
<code>src/app/api/*</code> for management/configuration APIs</li>
<li>Next rewrites in <code>next.config.mjs</code> map <code>/v1/*</code> to <code>/api/v1/*</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Important compatibility routes:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts</code></li>

<p>OmniRoute can install, supervise, and route to locally-running AI tool processes
called <strong>embedded services</strong>. Two are shipped in v3.8.4: 9Router and CLIProxyAPI.</p>
<p>Architecture layers:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<strong>UI</strong> (<code>/dashboard/providers/services</code>) — two-tab page with lifecycle controls,
live log streaming, API key management, and (for 9Router) embedded native UI via
an internal reverse proxy.</li>
<li>
<strong>API</strong> (<code>/api/services/{name}/*</code>) — 8 endpoints for 9Router, 7 for CLIProxyAPI,
all classified <strong>LOCAL_ONLY</strong> (hard rule #17). A shared <code>GET /api/services/[name]/logs</code>
SSE endpoint serves both services.</li>
<li>
<strong>Supervisor</strong> (<code>src/lib/services/</code>) — generic <code>ServiceSupervisor</code> class wraps
<code>child_process.spawn</code>, holds a 5 MB ring buffer for SSE log streaming, a health
probe loop, an atomic operation lock, and a SIGTERM→SIGKILL graceful shutdown.
<code>bootstrap.ts</code> wires all configured services at process start.</li>
<li>
<strong>Provider/executor</strong> (<code>open-sse/executors/ninerouter.ts</code>) — 9Router is exposed as
a real provider. Models are prefixed <code>9router/{sub}/{model}</code> and synced every 5 min
from 9Router's <code>/v1/models</code> endpoint.</li>
</ul>
<p>Deep-dive: <code>docs/frameworks/EMBEDDED-SERVICES.md</code></p>

<div class="markdown-heading"><h3 class="heading-element">A. Auto Combo Engine</h3><a id="user-content-a-auto-combo-engine" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: A. Auto Combo Engine" href="#a-auto-combo-engine"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p>Auto Combo dynamically scores and picks routing targets at request time, rather than
relying on a static combo definition. It powers the <code>auto/*</code> model prefix family.</p>
<ul>
<li>Engine entry: <code>open-sse/services/autoCombo/</code> (<code>autoComboEngine.ts</code>,
<code>scoringEngine.ts</code>, <code>virtualFactory.ts</code>, <code>modePacks.ts</code>)</li>
<li>Resolver: <code>src/domain/comboResolver.ts</code> (auto-detection of <code>auto/</code> prefix)</li>
<li>Dashboard: <code>/dashboard/auto-combo</code>
</li>
<li>Telemetry: <code>auto_combo_decisions</code> SQLite table</li>
</ul>
<p>Key capabilities:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<strong>14 routing strategies</strong> (priority, weighted, fill-first, round-robin, P2C, random,
least-used, cost-optimized, strict-random, <strong>auto</strong>, lkgp, context-optimized,
context-relay, plus a fallback path) — auto is the headline addition in v3.8.0.</li>
<li>
<strong>9-factor scoring</strong>: cost, latency p95, success rate, quota headroom, lockout
proximity, breaker state, recent failures, model availability, and tag affinity.</li>
<li>
<strong>Virtual factory</strong> materializes ephemeral combos when no matching named combo
exists, sourcing candidates from healthy active provider connections.</li>
<li>
<strong>Auto prefixes</strong>: <code>auto/coding</code>, <code>auto/cheap</code>, <code>auto/fast</code>, <code>auto/offline</code>,
<code>auto/smart</code>, <code>auto/lkgp</code> — each backed by a tuned weight profile.</li>
<li>
<strong>4 mode packs</strong>: coding, fast, cheap, smart — shipped as preset weight
configurations callable from the dashboard.</li>
</ul>
<p>For full algorithmic detail (factor formulas, weight tuning), see
<a href="../routing/AUTO-COMBO.md"><code>docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md</code></a>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading"><h3 class="heading-element">C. Guardrails</h3><a id="user-content-c-guardrails" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: C. Guardrails" href="#c-guardrails"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p>The guardrails module is a hot-reloadable middleware layer that inspects requests
and responses for PII, prompt injection, and unsafe vision content. Violations
short-circuit the request with HTTP <strong>503</strong> plus a structured error code, allowing
downstream callers to retry or branch.</p>
<ul>
<li>Module root: <code>src/lib/guardrails/</code> (<code>base.ts</code>, <code>registry.ts</code>, <code>piiMasker.ts</code>,
<code>promptInjection.ts</code>, <code>visionBridge.ts</code>, <code>visionBridgeHelpers.ts</code>)</li>
<li>Hot reload: registry watches for config changes and rebuilds the chain in place</li>
<li>Wire-in points: chat handler entry, image generation handler, response sanitizer</li>
<li>HTTP contract: violations surface as <code>503</code> with <code>error.code = "GUARDRAIL_VIOLATION"</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>For ruleset authoring and threshold tuning, see
<a href="../security/GUARDRAILS.md"><code>docs/security/GUARDRAILS.md</code></a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading"><h3 class="heading-element">D. Domain Layer</h3><a id="user-content-d-domain-layer" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: D. <p>The <code>src/domain/</code> namespace centralizes policy decisions so route handlers do not
have to assemble lockout/budget/fallback logic themselves.</p>
<ul>
<li>Policy engine: <code>src/domain/policyEngine.ts</code> — single entry point for
pre-execution evaluation (lockout → budget → fallback ordering)</li>
<li>Cost rules: <code>src/domain/costRules.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Fallback policy: <code>src/domain/fallbackPolicy.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Lockout policy: <code>src/domain/lockoutPolicy.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Tag-based routing: <code>src/domain/tagRouter.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Combo resolver: <code>src/domain/comboResolver.ts</code> — resolves combo names, auto/*
prefixes, and wildcard model targets to concrete execution plans</li>
<li>Connection/model rule joiner: <code>src/domain/connectionModelRules.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Model availability snapshots: <code>src/domain/modelAvailability.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Provider expiration tracking: <code>src/domain/providerExpiration.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Quota cache: <code>src/domain/quotaCache.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Degradation state: <code>src/domain/degradation.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Configuration audit: <code>src/domain/configAudit.ts</code>
</li>
<li>OmniRoute response metadata builder: <code>src/domain/omnirouteResponseMeta.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Assessment subsystem: <code>src/domain/assessment/</code> — periodic evaluation jobs</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading"><h3 class="heading-element">E. Authorization Pipeline</h3><a id="user-content-e-authorization-pipeline" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: E. Authorization Pipeline" href="#e-authorization-pipeline"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p>The authorization pipeline classifies every incoming request and applies the
appropriate policy chain before dispatch.</p>
<ul>
<li>Pipeline entry: <code>src/server/authz/pipeline.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Request classifier: <code>src/server/authz/classify.ts</code> — distinguishes public
compatibility routes from management routes</li>
<li>Public route inventory: <code>src/shared/constants/publicApiRoutes.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Policies: <code>src/server/authz/policies/</code> — composable predicates
(<code>requireApiKey</code>, <code>requireManagement</code>, <code>requireFreshAuth</code>, etc.)</li>
<li>Header utilities: <code>src/server/authz/headers.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Assertion helper: <code>src/server/authz/assertAuth.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Request context: <code>src/server/authz/context.ts</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Public vs management routes are a hard boundary: agent/cooldown APIs and
provider mutations require management auth (HTTP 401 if missing).</p>
<p>For the full route classification rules, see
<a href="./AUTHZ_GUIDE.md"><code>docs/architecture/AUTHZ_GUIDE.md</code></a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading"><h3 class="heading-element">F. Workflow FSM and Task-Aware Router</h3><a id="user-content-f-workflow-fsm-and-task-aware-router" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: F. Workflow FSM and Task-Aware Router" href="#f-workflow-fsm-and-task-aware-router"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p>A finite-state-machine driven router layered above combo selection to direct
traffic based on the detected workflow stage (planning, execution,
review) and background-task affinity.</p>
<ul>
<li>Workflow FSM: <code>open-sse/services/workflowFSM.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Task-aware router: <code>open-sse/services/taskAwareRouter.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Background task detector: <code>open-sse/services/backgroundTaskDetector.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Intent classifier: <code>open-sse/services/intentClassifier.ts</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>The FSM transitions feed into Auto Combo's scoring, biasing toward cheaper models
for background/automation tasks and toward stronger models for interactive
planning/review turns.</p>

<p>Several providers ship dedicated resilience and stealth modules that piggy-back on
the global circuit breaker / connection cooldown / model lockout layers:</p>
<ul>
<li>Antigravity 429 engine: <code>open-sse/services/antigravity429Engine.ts</code> (rotates
identity, scrubs response headers, drives credits/version tracking via
<code>antigravityCredits.ts</code>, <code>antigravityHeaderScrub.ts</code>, <code>antigravityHeaders.ts</code>,
<code>antigravityIdentity.ts</code>, <code>antigravityObfuscation.ts</code>, <code>antigravityVersion.ts</code>)</li>
<li>ModelScope quota policy: <code>open-sse/services/modelscopePolicy.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Claude Code CCH (Compatibility Channel Handshake): <code>open-sse/services/claudeCodeCCH.ts</code>,
plus <code>claudeCodeCompatible.ts</code>, <code>claudeCodeConstraints.ts</code>, <code>claudeCodeExtraRemap.ts</code>,
<code>claudeCodeToolRemapper.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Claude Code fingerprint shaping: <code>open-sse/services/claudeCodeFingerprint.ts</code>
</li>
<li>Claude Code obfuscation: <code>open-sse/services/claudeCodeObfuscation.ts</code>
</li>
<li>ChatGPT TLS client: <code>open-sse/services/chatgptTlsClient.ts</code> (curl-impersonate
style for ChatGPT-Web sessions)</li>
<li>ChatGPT image cache: <code>open-sse/services/chatgptImageCache.ts</code>
</li>
</ul>
<p>For the full stealth playbook and operational guidance, see
<a href="../security/STEALTH_GUIDE.md"><code>docs/security/STEALTH_GUIDE.md</code></a>.</p>

<p>Primary state DB (SQLite):</p>
<ul>
<li>Core infra: <code>src/lib/db/core.ts</code> (better-sqlite3, migrations, WAL)</li>
<li>Re-export facade: <code>src/lib/localDb.ts</code> (thin compatibility layer for callers)</li>
<li>file: <code>${DATA_DIR}/storage.sqlite</code> (or <code>$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omniroute/storage.sqlite</code> when set, else <code>~/.omniroute/storage.sqlite</code>)</li>
<li>entities (tables + KV namespaces): providerConnections, providerNodes, modelAliases, combos, apiKeys, settings, pricing, <strong>customModels</strong>, <strong>proxyConfig</strong>, <strong>ipFilter</strong>, <strong>thinkingBudget</strong>, <strong>systemPrompt</strong>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Usage persistence:</p>
<ul>
<li>facade: <code>src/lib/usageDb.ts</code> (decomposed modules in <code>src/lib/usage/*</code>)</li>
<li>SQLite tables in <code>storage.sqlite</code>: <code>usage_history</code>, <code>call_logs</code>, <code>proxy_logs</code>
</li>
<li>optional file artifacts remain for compatibility/debug (<code>${DATA_DIR}/log.txt</code>, <code>${DATA_DIR}/call_logs/</code>, <code><repo>/logs/...</code>)</li>
<li>legacy JSON files are migrated to SQLite by startup migrations when present</li>
</ul>
<p>Domain State DB (SQLite):</p>
<ul>
<li>
<code>src/lib/db/domainState.ts</code> — CRUD operations for domain state</li>
<li>Tables (created in <code>src/lib/db/core.ts</code>): <code>domain_fallback_chains</code>, <code>domain_budgets</code>, <code>domain_cost_history</code>, <code>domain_lockout_state</code>, <code>domain_circuit_breakers</code>
</li>
<li>Write-through cache pattern: in-memory Maps are authoritative at runtime; mutations are written synchronously to SQLite; state is restored from DB on cold start</li>
</ul>

    Sync->>DB: set cloudEnabled=true
    Sync->>DB: ensure API key exists
    Sync->>Cloud: POST /sync/{machineId} (providers/aliases/combos/keys)
    Cloud-->>Sync: sync result
    Sync->>Cloud: GET /{machineId}/v1/verify
    Sync-->>UI: enabled + verification status

    UI->>Sync: POST action=sync
    Sync->>Cloud: POST /sync/{machineId}
    Cloud-->>Sync: remote data
    Sync->>DB: update newer local tokens/status
    Sync-->>UI: synced

    UI->>Sync: POST action=disable
    Sync->>DB: set cloudEnabled=false
    Sync->>Cloud: DELETE /sync/{machineId}
    Sync->>Claude: switch ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL back to local (if needed)
    Sync-->>UI: disabled
</pre>
    </div></div></section>

<p>Periodic sync is triggered by <code>CloudSyncScheduler</code> when cloud is enabled.</p>

<p>Detected source formats include:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>openai</code></li>
<li><code>openai-responses</code></li>
<li><code>claude</code></li>
<li><code>gemini</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Target formats include:</p>
<ul>
<li>OpenAI chat/Responses</li>
<li>Claude</li>
<li>Gemini/Gemini-CLI/Antigravity envelope</li>
<li>Kiro</li>
<li>Cursor</li>
</ul>
<p>Translations use <strong>OpenAI as the hub format</strong> — all conversions go through OpenAI as intermediate:</p>

<p>Translations are selected dynamically based on source payload shape and provider target format.</p>
<p>Additional processing layers in the translation pipeline:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<strong>Response sanitization</strong> — Strips non-standard fields from OpenAI-format responses (both streaming and non-streaming) to ensure strict SDK compliance</li>
<li>
<strong>Role normalization</strong> — Converts <code>developer</code> → <code>system</code> for non-OpenAI targets; merges <code>system</code> → <code>user</code> for models that reject the system role (GLM, ERNIE)</li>
<li>
<strong>Think tag extraction</strong> — Parses <code><think>...</think></code> blocks from content into <code>reasoning_content</code> field</li>
<li>
<strong>Structured output</strong> — Converts OpenAI <code>response_format.json_schema</code> to Gemini's <code>responseMimeType</code> + <code>responseSchema</code>
</li>
</ul>

<p>Runtime visibility sources:</p>
<ul>
<li>console logs from <code>src/sse/utils/logger.ts</code>
</li>
<li>per-request usage aggregates in SQLite (<code>usage_history</code>, <code>call_logs</code>, <code>proxy_logs</code>)</li>
<li>four-stage detailed payload captures in SQLite (<code>request_detail_logs</code>) when <code>settings.detailed_logs_enabled=true</code>
</li>
<li>textual request status log in <code>log.txt</code> (optional/compat)</li>
<li>optional application log files under <code>logs/</code> when <code>APP_LOG_TO_FILE=true</code>
</li>
<li>optional request artifacts under <code>${DATA_DIR}/call_logs/</code> when the call log pipeline is enabled</li>
<li>dashboard usage endpoints (<code>/api/usage/*</code>) for UI consumption</li>
</ul>
<p>Detailed request payload capture stores up to four JSON payload stages per routed call:</p>
<ul>
<li>raw request received from the client</li>
<li>translated request actually sent upstream</li>
<li>provider response reconstructed as JSON; streamed responses are compacted to the final summary plus stream metadata</li>
<li>final client response returned by OmniRoute; streamed responses are stored in the same compact summary form</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading"><h2 class="heading-element">Security-Sensitive Boundaries</h2><a id="user-content-security-sensitive-boundaries" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security-Sensitive Boundaries" href="#security-sensitive-boundaries"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<ol>
<li>
<code>usageDb</code> and <code>localDb</code> share the same base directory policy (<code>DATA_DIR</code> -> <code>XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omniroute</code> -> <code>~/.omniroute</code>) with legacy file migration.</li>
<li>
<code>/api/v1/route.ts</code> delegates to the same unified catalog builder used by <code>/api/v1/models</code> (<code>src/app/api/v1/models/catalog.ts</code>) to avoid semantic drift.</li>
<li>Request logger writes full headers/body when enabled; treat log directory as sensitive.</li>
<li>Cloud behavior depends on correct <code>NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL</code> and cloud endpoint reachability.</li>
<li>The <code>open-sse/</code> directory is published as the <code>@omniroute/open-sse</code> <strong>npm workspace package</strong>. Source code imports it via <code>@omniroute/open-sse/...</code> (resolved by Next.js <code>transpilePackages</code>). File paths in this document still use the directory name <code>open-sse/</code> for consistency.</li>
<li>Charts in the dashboard use <strong>Recharts</strong> (SVG-based) for accessible, interactive analytics visualizations (model usage bar charts, provider breakdown tables with success rates).</li>
<li>E2E tests use <strong>Playwright</strong> (<code>tests/e2e/</code>), run via <code>npm run test:e2e</code>. Unit tests use <strong>Node.js test runner</strong> (<code>tests/unit/</code>), run via <code>npm run test:unit</code>. Source code under <code>src/</code> is <strong>TypeScript</strong> (<code>.ts</code>/<code>.tsx</code>); the <code>open-sse/</code> workspace remains JavaScript (<code>.js</code>).</li>
<li>Settings page is organized into 7 tabs: General, Appearance, AI, Security, Routing, Resilience, Advanced. The Resilience page only configures request queue, connection cooldown, provider breaker, and wait-for-cooldown behavior; live breaker runtime state is shown on the Health page.</li>
<li>
<strong>Context Relay</strong> strategy (<code>context-relay</code>) is split across two layers: <code>combo.ts</code> decides if a handoff should be generated, <code>chat.ts</code> injects the handoff after account resolution. Handoff data lives in <code>context_handoffs</code> SQLite table. This split is intentional because only <code>chat.ts</code> knows whether the actual account changed.</li>
<li>
<strong>Proxy enforcement</strong> is now comprehensive: <code>tokenHealthCheck.ts</code> resolves proxy per connection, <code>/api/providers/validate</code> uses <code>runWithProxyContext</code>, and <code>proxyFetch.ts</code> uses <code>undici.fetch()</code> to maintain dispatcher compatibility on Node 22.</li>
<li>
<strong>Node.js runtime policy detection</strong>: <code>/api/settings/require-login</code> returns <code>nodeVersion</code> and <code>nodeCompatible</code> fields. The login page renders a warning banner when the runtime falls outside the supported secure Node.js lines.</li>
</ol>
